title: Gravity is getting a more expensive-looking wardrobe.
description: Sling Nouveau is becoming Sling Bling. New artwork, twenty world paintings, and an ambitious campaign are on the workbench.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: On the workbench
paragraphs: Sling Nouveau is becoming Sling Bling. The overhaul is aiming for 1,000 levels, gold-and-jewel animal-inspired currency creatures, coins, special balls, and elegant city backdrops. Apparently knocking things over can have excellent taste.

Twenty background paintings and new creature artwork have been created. The artwork is ready for a look; the game still has work to do. Physics testing is incomplete, and the overhaul has not been released.
We want the shot to feel as good as the scenery looks. Gravity remains a demanding collaborator.

title: A little gold trim. The same difficult discard.
description: Gin Rummy has a new glossy 4OH calling card. Better tailoring does not guarantee better decisions.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: On the workbench
paragraphs: Gin Rummy has a new calling card: a glossy 4OH badge, gold trim, and the five, six, and seven of hearts. The tile has been built and checked in the development version. Those three cards have coordinated their appearance rather better than some of our hands.
The game’s appeal remains the quiet contest between two players: build useful combinations, watch the discards, and decide when to knock.
This is a visual development update, not a public launch. Better tailoring does not guarantee better decisions. We checked.

title: A bedtime notification should know the way home.
description: A notification-to-Home navigation fix is in development testing. Fewer detours at the end of the day.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: On the workbench
paragraphs: Sleep Amigo’s notification-to-Home fix has been built and installed in development testing. A tap should take you where you meant to go, especially when your remaining enthusiasm for navigation is approximately zero.
It is a small piece of a bigger goal: make available sleep information easier to understand and offer a useful starting point for the evening.
Sleep Amigo remains in development. It is a wellness companion, not medical care. The navigation is allowed to improve without acquiring a medical degree.

title: The scenic route has teeth.
description: A dragon to raise, a world to explore, and a travelling companion who should not sit beside the picnic basket.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: GildenSpire’s design starts with a dragon worth raising and a world worth flying through. Climbing, banking, diving, and exploring are meant to be part of the pleasure, well before another dragon develops territorial opinions. Our route planning is very confident for a group with this many teeth.
Different dragon shapes, movement, and abilities are part of the creative direction. Choosing a creature should matter beyond its paintwork.
This is a look at the game we are building, not a launch announcement. The sky is ambitious. The release date remains unannounced. We are packing optimism. It is lighter than spare wings.

title: The last card has declined to comment.
description: Three layers of cards. One very good plan. We should probably have told the deck about the plan.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Palace asks you to clear your hand, work through the face-up reserve, and then confront the cards you cannot see. An excellent arrangement for anyone who enjoys making a plan and having the deck review it. We usually have a splendid strategy right up until the cards arrive.
The complete website game offers local play against a bot. The separate app remains in private testing, with online development work distinct from that browser table.

Readable choices, useful power cards, and a finish that refuses to reveal its references in advance. The website table is available to play; this spotlight does not announce a standalone app release. Our confidence is coming along beautifully. The deck has requested a second opinion.

title: Just popping to the bakery. Eventually.
description: A quick trip to the bakery, with just a small detour through the rest of the entire town.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: BooYang City’s premise is a neighborhood full of different reasons to wander. The bakery, zoo, boutique, school, and hospital each give the city another kind of activity. We only meant to collect a loaf. We seem to have become emotionally invested in the zoo.
Explore somewhere, play, improve it, and discover another destination. A short errand can develop a remarkably flexible itinerary.

Development continues; no public release is announced. The bakery is not accepting complaints about how long you spent at the zoo. You can explain the three-hour bread run when you get home. We will be very sympathetic.

title: Earth has assigned this to your thumb.
description: One small interceptor, an entire planet, and a thumb that was hoping for a quieter afternoon.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Thumb Command puts the Blueguard interceptor between an alien invasion and the city below. A small spacecraft, a large responsibility, and presumably a very interesting insurance renewal. We would have sent a larger committee, but the spacecraft has limited seating.
The design favors readable action, distinctive enemies, and an interface that leaves room for the fighting. If the city needs defending, the controls should not demand a separate briefing.

This is a spotlight on its arcade-defense premise, not a report of newly released missions or features. Thumb Command remains in development. We appreciate your help. The planet is a little difficult to replace.

title: Prepare a position before inventing one aloud.
description: A little preparation now. Fewer brilliant things to say arriving on the drive home.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: SOVINTO is being developed around negotiation preparation: what you want, what matters most, and where you have room to move. Remembering these things before the conversation is generally more convenient than remembering them in the parking lot afterward. Our best arguments have a terrible habit of turning up when the meeting is over.
The current foundation includes local case preparation and general, prewritten help. Interactive practice, a broader toolset, and live AI coaching remain development work.

Preparation cannot guarantee agreement. It can at least give “let me think” something useful to do. SOVINTO remains in development. We are very persuasive in the car afterward. We would like to move some of that talent into the meeting.

title: Some gifts come with thirteen points.
description: Passing cards with a lovely smile. Letting the recipient discover the problem in their own time.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Four players. No partners. Plenty to notice. Hearts makes a passing decision feel generous right up until the recipient examines it. We like to include a smile with the three cards. It is the least we can do under the circumstances.
The current app supports complete local games with three bots and remains in internal testing. Online tables are still being developed.

A readable hand, clear turns, and an understandable table matter. The queen of spades already supplies enough tension. She does not need help from the interface. We are working on being gracious. We would also very much like to win.

title: The buildings would like to express themselves.
description: A town with room for your ideas. Even the one that requires moving the bakery again.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Funky Town’s creative direction gives ordinary buildings rather extraordinary prospects. Murals, gardens, music, sculpture, and unusual architecture belong in a town shaped by the player. Our city planning is coming along nicely, provided nobody asks why the bakery has moved three times.
Grow a neighborhood, change its character, and zoom out to see your choices add up. Sensible shoes may be advisable. Sensible buildings are negotiable.

Development continues; this is not an announcement that new building tools or public community features have shipped. There is room for a sensible neighborhood. We have also made room for your other idea.

title: The bread has established a defensive perimeter.
description: One determined bread dinosaur. One Breadstone. A defense plan that has risen to the occasion.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Bobby has a herd to protect and a Breadstone to defend. The proposed solution involves upgraded towers, thoughtful placement, and considerably more military preparation than most baked goods receive. Most bread is happy with a basket. Bobby has opted for a more comprehensive security arrangement.
The artwork and battlefield should make the world inviting while keeping the action easy to follow.

Bobby remains in development, with no public release date announced. This is a closer look at the idea, not a claim that a fresh batch of levels has shipped. Please admire the fortifications. Someone has put a lot of heart into this loaf.

title: Doom has arrived. The village has objections.
description: Two siblings, a village to protect, and an intruder who has clearly ignored the welcome mat.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: A brother and sister defend the village that shelters them. Choose a sibling, build and upgrade defenses, and stand against Girmat’s advancing monsters. The village is usually quite welcoming. It is making an exception for the advancing monsters.
The two heroes belong to one game. Distinctive towers give a village facing Doom options beyond “another slightly different cannon.”

Development continues; no public release is announced. Girmat’s alarming presentation should not be mistaken for an approved launch schedule. We have tried being hospitable. The towers are handling the follow-up.

title: A rescue operation with very little subtlety.
description: A rescue plan with sparkles. Our sensible little match has invited half the board.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Suit matching, combos, crystal cages, and unicorn rescue make a successful chain reaction both useful and agreeably excessive. We had intended a modest little combo. Apparently it invited its relatives.
Clarity matters underneath the spectacle: understand the board and tools, then enjoy what happens when a good decision sets everything moving.

The game remains in development. Unicorn Blast is the current name; older pages may still mention HeartStack. This spotlight introduces no new release. The unicorns are simply receiving their allotted editorial attention. Restraint was discussed. The unicorns voted for the sparkling option.

title: Your bid has been noted by another person.
description: Your partner believes in you. A touching development, considering what you just bid.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Two partners must turn their bids into a result. Count the tricks, watch the bags, and consider how impressive your confidence will sound if someone else has to rescue it. We said it with such confidence. We would now appreciate a little cooperation from the hand.
Local bot play, including a bot partner, is implemented in the app under internal testing. Public multiplayer is not yet available.

Partnership strategy should provide the complexity. Finding the score should not. This is a developer spotlight, rather than a new release announcement. We bring optimism to the partnership. Our partner would quite reasonably prefer tricks.

title: Royal duties include moving that chair again.
description: Style, cook, decorate, and move that chair again. The royal household is being very patient.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Character styling, castle rooms, cooking, and decorating share one creative-simulation premise. Choose how things look, try another arrangement, and decide the first arrangement was right after all. We were certain about that chair five minutes ago. The royal household has kindly agreed not to mention it.
Outfit fit, layering, and expressive characters matter when making choices is the main event.

This is a spotlight, not a newly released wardrobe or room collection. Development continues, and the royal calendar contains no public launch date. The crown confers many privileges. Instant certainty about curtains is, sadly, not one of them.

title: A useful introduction starts before “Hello.”
description: A little useful context before hello. We recommend learning the name before practising the handshake.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Whomly is being designed to turn public professional information into context you can actually use: who fits a search, what supports that fit, and what might make a thoughtful introduction. We are aiming for a thoughtful introduction, rather than the spectacular panic of realizing we have forgotten the name.
The proposed flow moves from discovery to understanding to preparation. It is user-directed research, not private-profile access or an imaginary dossier on somebody’s inner life.

Whomly remains in development; no public service or automated contact feature is announced. Research should improve the conversation, not give everyone a reason to leave it. A little preparation can do wonders. We still recommend checking for spinach before the meeting.

title: A meeting for one. Excellent attendance.
description: A table for one. Your opponent has cancelled, which is awkward, because it's also you.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Uncover a card, find a useful move, and bring a little order to the deal. The development app includes different ways to play and a locally saved deal. We have cleared our schedule and asked everyone to keep the interruptions down. There is nobody else here.
Its personal challenge rating stays on the device; it is not a public leaderboard. Comfortable card sizes, clear presentation, and smooth movement set the direction.

The standalone app remains in development. No need to schedule a rematch with anyone, which does simplify the administration. If you need another deal, we understand. We were just about to suggest the same thing.

title: The habitat is ready for another opinion.
description: A home for your unicorn and your latest decorating idea. The last latest idea was also very good.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Personalize unicorns, shape habitats, decorate, discover, and enjoy mini-games along the way. The garden was finished. Then we saw another flower. You understand.
This is separate from Unicorn Blast: make a place feel yours, with the entirely reasonable possibility of reconsidering the mane after finishing the garden.

The game remains in development, with no public release date announced. Landscaping expertise is optional. Opinions about flowers will probably emerge naturally. We will be delighted to see what you make. We may ask where you found that particularly nice shrub.

title: Five cards can support a very large opinion.
description: Five cards and a brave decision. We have made longer speeches with considerably less evidence.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: Calling trump, recognizing the bowers, trusting a partner, and occasionally deciding you can manage without one. A brave conclusion for such a small handful of evidence. We are very sure about calling trump. This confidence is available in advance of the results.
Complete local bot matches are implemented in the app under internal testing; online tables remain development work.

Keep trump, the caller, partners, and scores easy to follow. The cards may surprise you; the controls should make an effort not to. If the brave plan works, we will be modest about it. We have been practising our expression.

title: An excellent result for your entirely random strategy.
description: Flip a card, enjoy a win, and accept the credit with modesty. The deck did quite a lot of the work.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: From the developers
paragraphs: War is a game of chance, and we see no reason to give the deck a management title. Flip the cards, settle the ties, and enjoy the result. We like a game where everyone can join in, including the person who has brought enthusiasm instead of a strategy.
The development app offers Classic, Quick, and Family Table play, including two to four people sharing one device. Match history and progress stay local; they are not an online skill ranking.

The standalone app remains in development. A good run is still worth enjoying, even if your strategic contribution was turning the card over. Please enjoy your good run. We will admire your technique and avoid asking too many questions.

title: Modern art has been informed about gravity.
description: Sling Nouveau begins with a pleasingly unreasonable idea: what if a sculptural playground also invited you to knock things down?

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Sling Nouveau begins with a pleasingly unreasonable idea: what if a sculptural playground also invited you to knock things down?
The immediate priority is the slingshot. It should be easy to grab, satisfying to pull, and simple to position. Your thumb should be planning the shot, not negotiating access to the controls.
We’re also exploring tougher materials and specialized balls, so choosing how to hit something becomes part of the fun.
First comes the feeling of a great shot. Then we give you increasingly interesting reasons to take another.

The browser work is focused on reliable play, readable cards, and a restart that takes you cleanly back to the beginning. We’re keeping the demo distinct from the broader Palace app.
A rematch should begin with a button, not a troubleshooting expedition.

We can aim for a friendlier experience. We cannot promise your friends will appreciate the queen of spades.

description: Spades deserves a table that respects the partnership.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Spades deserves a table that respects the partnership.
The bid, the score, the current trick, and your next action should be easy to understand. Everything else needs a good reason to occupy the screen.
Our design target is the rhythm of a satisfying card game: read the situation, make the decision, watch it unfold, and quietly reconsider how confident you sounded earlier.
The cards should provide the suspense. Finding the right button should not.

The current direction is cleaner presentation, more comfortable card sizes, and smoother movement. The board should feel calm without looking asleep.
We’re giving the classic its own polished place in the 4OH family.

The development priority is getting that basic rhythm right: stable play, readable cards, and battles that feel lively rather than sluggish.
The competition should come from what turns over—not from whether the interface cooperates.
Broader online ambitions remain development work unless verified. For now, the brief is wonderfully direct: make the familiar game feel good.

The current direction puts the emphasis on easier flight, clearer combat controls, a world worth moving through, and fire that deserves the name.
We’re pushing away from crowded controls and routine busywork toward the pleasure of going somewhere spectacular and doing something distinctly dragon-shaped when you arrive.
Progression should support that experience, not bury it under errands.
Online dragon-versus-dragon combat remains an ambition to develop—not a feature to announce before it works.

The exciting decisions should happen in the defense of the world, not in an overcrowded strip of controls.
A busy spaceship is good. A busy interface needs to make its case.

The workbench priorities include richer battlefield detail, useful close-up zoom, more expressive placement areas, and a cleaner way to choose and understand upgrades.
We want players thinking, “What does that one do?”

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: The Amigo is the point.
We’re shaping a sleep companion that can react to the information actually available, offer a useful observation, and sound like someone you would willingly hear from in the morning.
That means clearer presentation, a more expressive pillow character, and commentary that can be warm and cheeky without making things up.
Available sleep-stage information should not be ignored just because a long-term pattern is still developing. Missing data should be acknowledged, not invented.
The aim is better understanding—not a diagnosis delivered by a pillow.

Who is relevant? What supports that conclusion? What would make a thoughtful next conversation?
We’re interested in a clearer path from discovery to understanding—not an impressive-looking pile of unexplained results.

A useful briefing should leave you better informed, not merely in possession of several more tabs.

title: Before the dragons, there were cards.
description: Before there were dragons to steer, cities to build, or unicorns requiring an unreasonable amount of creative attention, there were cards.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: Before there were dragons to steer, cities to build, or unicorns requiring an unreasonable amount of creative attention, there were cards.

Palace, Hearts, Spades, and Euchre gave Four of Hearts its starting table. Familiar games. Different personalities. Plenty of opportunities to discover that “just make the cards work” is not, technically speaking, a development plan.

The important questions were wonderfully ordinary. Can you read your hand? Do you know whose turn it is? Does the game explain itself without delivering a lecture? Can you get to the enjoyable part before your tea becomes a historical artifact?
Those questions still follow us into every new project.
Four of Hearts became 4OH when the name was said out loud. No encrypted founder prophecy. No seventeen-slide branding revelation. Just a name that sounded right.
The ambitions have grown considerably. The basic test has not: does this feel good to use, and is it worth coming back for?
Pull up a chair. This is where the workbench story begins.

title: The card table got a little out of hand.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: A sensible studio might add another card game and call it a productive afternoon.
Our workbench now includes dragons, defensive towers, a heroic dinosaur, princess wardrobes, entire towns, and several unicorn-related responsibilities.
The card table did not disappear. It acquired some very unusual neighbors.

The expanding lineup has brought different design problems with it. A card game needs clarity and rhythm. A flying dragon needs convincing movement. A creative world needs room to explore. A princess wardrobe needs the shoes to maintain a professional relationship with the feet.
These are not interchangeable problems, and the games should not feel like the same template wearing different hats.
What connects them is the aim: make the interaction inviting, the personality memorable, and the next thing you want to do obvious.
We are building a family of games, not a warehouse of icons.
Somewhere along the way, the workbench became a neighborhood. Apparently we are responsible for the zoning now.

title: A U has entered the chat.
description: A brief developer detour into Canadian English, where “colour” brings an extra letter and “centre” rearranges the furniture.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: A brief developer detour into Canadian English, where “colour” brings an extra letter and “centre” rearranges the furniture.
We like this. Even the spelling gets a little customization.

Canadian English often keeps the U in words such as “colour” and “favour,” while favoring endings such as “centre” and “theatre.” That does not make it a separate language, and it certainly does not mean every Canadian writes exactly the same way.
It does give a software studio something entertaining to think about between moving buttons three pixels to the left.
There is a real design point hiding under the extra vowel: words should feel natural to the people reading them. A label is not finished merely because it fits in a rectangle.
Our preferred international policy is straightforward: make people welcome, make the instructions clear, and never charge extra for the U.
That would be a microtransactioun.

title: Fewer buttons. More “one more go.”
description: The workbench has a recurring request: give the enjoyable part more room.

body.heading: From the workshop
paragraphs: The workbench has a recurring request: give the enjoyable part more room.

More room for the dragon to fly. More room for the city to feel like a city. More room to see the cards. More room to pull back a slingshot without conducting a delicate archaeological excavation with your thumb.
This is not a campaign against useful features. It is a campaign against making every useful feature stand in the doorway at once.
Across the projects, the direction is clearer controls, calmer screens, more expressive artwork, and interactions that make sense before an instruction panel starts clearing its throat.
The same principle applies to our apps. Sleep information should feel understandable. Research should become useful context. Preparation should make a difficult conversation less difficult.
A screen does not earn its keep by containing more things.
It earns its keep when you know what to do next—and actually want to do it.

title: AI in the workshop—and in useful products

body.heading: September 12: a note from the workbench

body.heading: Two different roles
paragraphs: AI-assisted development does not mean every product contains an AI engine. Whomly includes an optional AI-assisted public research and briefing workflow. paragraphs: SOVINTO’s aim is practical: prepare for conversations such as a new job offer or buying a house, then find useful guidance when you need it. body.heading: Still on the workbench
paragraphs: Funky Town’s next city-building and creativity-pressure redesign is also in progress. We will share completed milestones as they are verified. Old-school values, modern ambitions, and careful engineering remain the thread through the work.

title: Introducing GildenSpire: Flight or Fight
description: Raise a dragon, take direct control in the sky, and discover what happens when flying becomes fighting.

body.heading: Considerably bigger wings
paragraphs: Four of Hearts Interactive is building something with considerably bigger wings.
GildenSpire begins with a simple idea: raise a dragon, climb onto its back, and discover what happens when the world stops being something you walk through and becomes something you fly over.

body.heading: Flying is gameplay
paragraphs: Raising your dragon matters. Training matters. Discovering new dragons matters. But the heart of GildenSpire is what happens once you take off.

You will climb, dive, bank through mountain passes, cross enormous landscapes, discover places hidden from the ground, and eventually encounter other creatures that are not particularly interested in sharing the sky.
Then flying becomes fighting.
That is GildenSpire.
Flight or fight.
And we are only beginning to build the world.

title: Why Flying Has to Be Fun
description: The journey should be gameplay: direct flight, enormous terrain, curiosity, and combat that rewards control.

body.heading: Getting somewhere should be part of the fun
paragraphs: There is a simple rule behind GildenSpire: getting somewhere should be part of the fun.
We do not want players to press a destination button and watch a dragon animation while the next screen loads.
We want you flying the dragon.

body.heading: Stay in the sky
paragraphs: We want mountains to feel enormous when you skim past them. We want diving toward an island to feel fast. We want you banking around towers, threading through ruins, climbing through clouds, and spotting something in the distance that makes you change direction just to see what it is.
And when combat begins, those same flying skills should matter.
A great dragon game should make you want to stay in the sky even when there is nowhere you are required to go.
That is one of the standards we are building GildenSpire around.

title: Building Dragons That Actually Feel Different

body.heading: Another dragon, not another skin
paragraphs: One red dragon, one blue dragon, one green dragon.
That is not enough.
GildenSpire is being designed around dragons that should actually feel different.
Different bodies. Different wings. Different movement. Different strengths. Different abilities. Different personalities.

body.heading: Different ways to fly and fight
paragraphs: A powerful fire dragon might feel heavy and aggressive in the air. A smaller air dragon might turn faster and climb differently. An ice dragon might completely change how a team approaches a fight.
The goal is not simply to collect another skin.
The goal is to discover another dragon.
And somewhere beyond all of them is the Golden Egg.

title: From Search to Opportunity: Building Whomly
description: How a search-first interface can turn public professional research into useful context and a thoughtful next step.

body.heading: Start with the question
paragraphs: Whomly begins with the person you are trying to find: a general counsel in Chicago, a healthcare innovation leader, a potential board member, or a specialist whose public work fits the problem in front of you.
The search interface is being designed to accept useful professional criteria without turning research into an endless directory.

body.heading: Public research, organized
paragraphs: The hard part is rarely finding one more public page. It is understanding why a person may be relevant. Whomly is designed to organize publicly available professional information into readable context, saved people, and lists the user controls.

AI-assisted summaries and outreach drafts may help with the work, but the boundary matters: public professional context in, user-reviewed preparation out. No private-profile access, automatic contact, or release date is being claimed.

paragraphs: Many city builders begin with different intentions and slowly converge on the same neat grid. Funky Town begins with the opposite question: what if progress made the place stranger, louder, and more personal?
Murals, graffiti, sculpture, music, unusual architecture, parks, studios, cafés, rooftop gardens, and gathering places can give each district a different identity.

paragraphs: The goal is not simply to make every building larger. It is to let players transform neighborhoods through creative decisions until two long-running Funky Towns could look dramatically different.
Community matters as much as colour. People and the places where they meet are what make the art feel alive. Funky Town is in development, with no public build or release date announced.

title: Press Ahead: a little head start.
description: A new expedition-inspired match-three game, with a name we could not possibly leave alone.
author: The 4OH Workshop

body.heading: On the workbench
paragraphs: Press Ahead is a new, separate match-three game in development, inspired by the Lewis and Clark expedition. It uses the Unicorn Blast project as its technical foundation; Unicorn Blast remains its own game.
The name comes with a small invitation: “press a head” and move ahead. We are trying to keep the wordplay under control. It has already packed a bag.

The private 0.2.0 developer-test candidate has 400 existing authored boards and 670 passing automated source tests. A standalone Android test package has been built and checked. Physical-phone testing and live sign-in/cloud checks still need their turn, and the newer recipe revision is not fully verified. This is progress from the workbench, not a public launch. We have plenty of trail ahead and a sensible amount of enthusiasm.
